source.title: Scaling Laws for Forgetting When Fine-Tuning Large Language Models

page_placements.theme: Transfer, adaptation and retention depend on source alignment and recipe

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-law analysis to fine-tuning, measuring fine-tuning loss and forgetting across LoRA ranks and update steps rather than measuring pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The study measures fine-tuning loss on OpenOrca and News, plus a separate forgetting metric, and fits both against fine-tuned parameter count and update steps. The ARC accuracy and safety-refusal results are not scaling-law measurements and are not included as rows. The pretraining scaling laws and other cited works are background, not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study fits a shifted power law of fine-tuning loss in LoRA parameter count and update steps for Llama 2 chat 7B on two datasets. That is a direct result on V5's fine-tuning regime. The forgetting-metric fits measure a different construct (cross-entropy to base-model predictions) and bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with three corrections. Forgetting is an inverse linear function of fine-tuning loss, and grows as a shifted power law in parameters fine-tuned and update steps. Fine-tuning loss itself follows a shifted power law similar to the pretraining laws of Kaplan and Henighan. Forgetting cannot be avoided by early stopping or by varying the number of parameters fine-tuned, and it degrades ARC reasoning and safety refusals.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes one pretrained Llama 2 chat model using LoRA and analyzes fine-tuning loss and a model-to-base prediction cross-entropy metric. It does not reproduce the original pretraining scaling-law measurements or compute-optimal allocation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the reported fit coefficients and exponents. For generalization to additional fine-tuning methods, the forgetting-versus-fine-tuning-loss fit and the joint parameter-and-step fit have different reported R² values.

fits_no_version.finding: Forgetting, measured as cross-entropy to the base model's predictions on WikiText-103, fits a shifted power law in fine-tuned parameters and update steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In LoRA fine-tuning, forgetting relative to the base model grows as a shifted power law in parameters fine-tuned and update steps.

fits_no_version.finding: Forgetting is an inverse linear function of fine-tuning loss on both datasets (R² .9450, .9736).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forgetting during fine-tuning is predicted mainly by the fine-tuning loss achieved.

fits_no_version.finding: On out-of-distribution fine-tuning methods, the forgetting fit based on P and N generalises much better than the fit based on fine-tuning loss alone (R² .8714 vs .1851).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forgetting fits that use parameter count and steps generalise across PEFT methods better than loss-only fits.

record.problems: The scaling experiments use one base model and two fine-tuning datasets. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The fine-tuning-loss fits are not held-out pretraining-loss measurements, and the additional-method analysis evaluates generalization of forgetting fits rather than pretraining scaling laws.
record.rows_left_out: ARC accuracy and safety-refusal outcomes in Section 4.2 are omitted because they are not reported as scaling-law results. The additional fine-tuning methods' individual parameter counts are not separate rows because the text gives no individual numerical loss or forgetting values for them.

untested.parts: Other modalities, repeated data and transfer are not tested. Fine-tuning is tested only with one 7B base model, two text datasets, and a narrow range (LoRA ranks 8–256, 50–260 steps), not several orders of magnitude.
Held-out pretraining loss is not measured.
Extrapolation of pretraining runs is not tested. Appendix B checks fine-tuning-loss fits on larger ranks only qualitatively.
Effects of model shape are not tested.
Downstream predictability from scale is not tested. ARC results are reported only for rank 8 checkpoints, not as a function of scale.
Fitting-choice dependence and curve bending are not tested. The two datasets give similar exponents, but no alternative fitting setups are compared.

missing.what: The fine-tuning-loss fit is said to predict fine-tuning loss for LoRA ranks 1000 and 2500 and full-model tuning, an extrapolation beyond the fitted range. Only a qualitative statement and a figure are given, with no numeric error.

record.verdict_notes: This is a single-author preprint from a company (Tenyx), with one base model and no uncertainty estimates. The fit form includes a large outer exponent ρ≈7.7 and very small inner exponents. The ARC and AdvBench results are not scale-dependent measurements and are rightly left out as rows.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger pretraining runs from fits on small pretraining runs.
Compute-optimal allocation between parameters and tokens, including its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study tests fine-tuning loss on two text datasets; it does not test held-out pretraining loss, other modalities, repeated data, or transfer.
Predictability of downstream task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
The study does not test compute-optimal splits, pretraining-law disagreements, or whether pretraining curves bend away from a power law.
